A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALDA study. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial layout changes and additional appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on four DMControl tasks, distribution-shift experiments, representation visualizations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Walker Walk experiments on latent dimensionality, critic gradients, and SVEA augmentation choices in Appendices A.9–A.11.

M1.justification: v2 Equation (7) moves StopGradient from the encoder output to the retrieved latent term, correcting the written commitment-loss gradient direction relative to v1 Equation (8). The architecture and association rule remain unchanged; this correction does not establish an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Appendix A.11 adds an actually used color-easy training environment for SVEA, with mild scene-color perturbations. The original four control tasks and color-hard/DistractingCS evaluation coverage remain.

E2.justification: Figure 17 adds SVEA (color easy) alongside ALDA and SVEA (image overlay). The original main comparison retains DARLA, SAC+AE, RePo, and SVEA; the newly cited bisimulation work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New Walker controls test latent dimensions 12, 32, 64, and 128, enable critic gradients through the encoder, and compare SVEA augmentation regimes. These extend experimental settings without replacing the original benchmark protocol or changing Table 1's hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Appendices A.9–A.11 substantially extend the diagnostic evidence with latent-dimensionality sensitivity, a critic-gradient ablation, and an augmentation-choice comparison. These address three additional questions on Walker Walk while retaining the previous temperature, framestacking, and representation analyses.

E5.justification: Existing plots retain their seed counts and confidence-interval reporting. Figures 15–16 use the already established four-seed averages and 95% bootstrapped intervals; no increased run count for retained results or new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figures 15–17 add substantial findings: 12-dimensional latents lead larger alternatives on training/color-hard; critic-gradient propagation reduces performance; and SVEA (color easy) trails ALDA on training/color-hard while performing similarly on DistractingCS. These are additional Walker results, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings. Existing benchmark and ablation curves are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit nonzero conditional-covariance condition to the weak-disentanglement definition, and Section 2.1 revises the SAC objective expressions. Theorem 1 and its Appendix A.1 proof remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions remain unchanged. However, the concluding Discussion replaces v1's statement that ALDA can use augmentation with an assertion that it scales with more data, and Section 5 adds conditional outperformance of SVEA under alternative augmentation.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving mismatch between latent dimensionality and source count, interference from critic gradients, and augmentation-dependent generalization. It also revises the Hopfield projection interpretation and adds interpretability/safety discussion. Existing temporal-representation and biological-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.8 adds forward-pass and associative-dynamics pseudocode. Section 5 more explicitly documents sampling and codebook-range interpolation for the retained latent visualizations. Architecture descriptions, Table 1 values, and the referenced SAC implementation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 and the bibliography add Zhang et al. (2021) on bisimulation-based invariant representations. This modestly extends the comparison with invariant-representation approaches without substantially changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify quantization, framestacking, association, and latent traversals. v2 adds an Impact Statement and reorganizes the implementation appendix, but the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with widespread figure resizing and relocation. v2 also adds Figures 15–17 and two algorithm boxes, and expands Figure 6's caption. Existing plots largely retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The additional Walker controls strengthen support for design choices, while pseudocode and the commitment-loss clarification improve reproducibility. The gain is limited: the new evidence concerns one task, and the broader data-scaling and real-world conclusions extend beyond what those tests establish.
